headline: Evolutionary models link protein epistasis, lineage dynamics and codon selection patterns
label: Molecular Evolution Inference Models
summary: Three 2026 studies apply continuous-time, Bayesian and codon-model frameworks to protein, B-cell and avian gene evolution.
synthesis: The dominant thread across these items is explicit, parameterized modelling of evolutionary processes fitted to sequence or lineage data. The protein study couples a Potts generative model to a continuous-time evolution process simulated by Gillespie algorithm, revealing epistatic signatures in protein evolution. TyCHE is a Bayesian phylogenetics package that infers time-resolved lineage trees with clock rates linked to discrete states, and its SimBLE simulator is applied to B cells and other heterogeneously evolving populations. The avian CYP4 study applies site, branch and branch-site codon models across four subfamilies in 363 genomes to relate selection patterns to lineage-specific evolution. The items differ in scope, and only the CYP4 study is a comparative genome analysis. What is new here is the pairing of epistasis-aware generative dynamics with time-resolved lineage inference, alongside codon-level selection scans across an avian genome set.
